fields.aka: Kedāranātha Datta, Saccidānanda Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākura, Kedarnath Datta, the Seventh Gosvāmī
fields.appearance: Bhādra Śukla Trayodaśī (Gauḍīya calendar); 2 September 1838 (18 Bhādra 1245), a Sunday, at Bīranagara (Ulā), Nadia
fields.disappearance: Āṣāḍha Amāvasyā, the day of Gadādhara Paṇḍita (Gauḍīya calendar); 23 June 1914
fields.place: Born at Bīranagara (Ulā), Nadia; Purī (1868-74; Bhakti-kuṭī from 1902); Calcutta (Bhakti-bhavana); Kṛṣṇanagara; Godruma, Navadvīpa (Svānanda-sukhada-kuñja)
fields.guru: Vipina-vihārī Gosvāmī (dīkṣā), Śrī Jagannātha dās Bābājī (śikṣā)
fields.disciples: Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Sarasvatī (his son; śikṣā), Gaura Kiśora dāsa bābājī (śikṣā)
fields.works: About a hundred books: Jaiva-dharma, Śrī Caitanya-śikṣāmṛta, Harināma-cintāmaṇi, Bhajana-rahasya, Śaraṇāgati, Gītāvalī, Gītamālā, Kalyāṇa-kalpataru, Datta-kaustubha, Kṛṣṇa-saṁhitā, Tattva-viveka, Āmnāya-sūtra, Daśa-mūla-śikṣā, Prema-pradīpa, Navadvīpa-dhāma-māhātmya, Bhakti-tattva-viveka; Rasika-rañjana (Gītā), Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya (Caitanya-caritāmṛta); The Bhāgavata: Its Philosophy, Its Ethics and Its Theology; Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu: His Life and Precepts; Svalikhita-jīvanī; the journal Sajjana-toṣaṇī (from 1881)
fields.notes: Son of Ānandacandra Datta and Jaganmohinī Devī (daughter of the zamindar Īśvaracandra Mustauphi of Bīranagara); wives: the daughter of Madhusūdana Mitra of Rāṇāghāṭa, then Bhāgavatī Devī; sons include Annadā Prasāda, Kamalā Prasāda, Bimala Prasāda (Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī), Varadā, Virajā and Lalitā Prasāda. Deputy magistrate of the British government; in charge of the Jagannātha temple at Purī (1868-74). Found Śrī Caitanya's birthplace at Māyāpura (1887-88), confirmed by Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī; began the Nāma-haṭṭa; called the Seventh Gosvāmī. Left the world on Gadādhara Paṇḍita's disappearance day, 1914.

fields.aka: Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura, Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Mahārāja, Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura Prabhupāda, Bimala Prasāda Datta, Siddhānta Sarasvatī
fields.appearance: Phālguna Kṛṣṇa Pañcamī (Gauḍīya calendar; Māgha kṛṣṇa pañcamī counting from new moon); 6 February 1874, at Jagannātha Purī
fields.disappearance: Pauṣa Kṛṣṇa Caturthī (Gauḍīya calendar); 1 January 1937, at Calcutta; samādhi at Śrī Caitanya Maṭha, Māyāpura
fields.place: Born at Jagannātha Purī; Calcutta (Bhakti-bhavana; Gauḍīya Maṭha, Bāghbāzār); Māyāpura (Śrī Caitanya Maṭha, his samādhi)
fields.guru: Gaura Kiśora dāsa bābājī (dīkṣā), Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura (śikṣā)
fields.works: Anubhāṣya on the Caitanya-caritāmṛta; Sūrya-siddhānta; Brāhmaṇa o Vaiṣṇava; many editions and commentaries; the papers Sajjana-toṣaṇī, The Harmonist, Gauḍīya, Bhāgavata (Hindi), Nadīyā Prakāśa (daily), Kīrtana, Paramārthī
fields.notes: Bimala Prasāda, son of Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura and Bhāgavatī Devī, born in Purī in 1874. Title Siddhānta Sarasvatī for his astronomy. Dīkṣā from Gaura Kiśora dāsa Bābājī at Godruma (1900); chanted a billion names at Māyāpura from 1905; defeated the smārtas at Midnapore (1911). Took tridaṇḍa-sannyāsa himself before his guru's picture at Māyāpura (1918). Founded the Gauḍīya Maṭha: sixty-four maṭhas in India, Rangoon and London; sent sannyāsīs to Europe (1933). Left the world on 1 January 1937 in Calcutta.

fields.guru: Śrīla Bhagavat dāsa Bābājī (bābājī veśa), Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura (śikṣā)
fields.disappearance: Kārtika Śukla Daśamī, the day of Utthāna Ekādaśī (Gauḍīya calendar), 1915, at Kuliyā (Navadvīpa town); samādhi moved in 1932 to Śrī Caitanya Maṭha, Māyāpura
fields.notes: Vaṁśī dāsa, a grain merchant of Vāgyāna near Ṭepākholā on the Padmā; after his wife's death took the bābājī dress from Bhāgavata dāsa Bābājī (disciple of Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī) and lived about thirty years in Vṛndāvana, then in Navadvīpa. Śikṣā from Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, from whom he heard the Bhāgavatam. Renunciation personified: wore cloth from the burning ghāṭ and lived on rice soaked in Gaṅgā water; refused the Mahārāja of Kāsimbāzār. His only disciple, Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (dīkṣā 1900), buried him at Kuliyā.

fields.disciples: Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura (śikṣā), Śrīla Bhagavat dāsa Bābājī (bābājī veśa), Bihārī dāsa (his servant)
fields.disappearance: Phālguna Śukla Pratipat (Gauḍīya calendar); 1894 (another text: 1895, Bengali 1302), at Koladvīpa (Navadvīpa town)
fields.notes: «Vaiṣṇava-sārvabhauma». Born in Mymensingh; disciple of Madhusūdana dāsa Bābājī of Sūrya-kuṇḍa, in the line of Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa through Uddhava dāsa (another text: disciple of Jagadānanda Gosvāmī of Śṛṅgāravaṭa, bābājī dress from Siddha Kṛṣṇadāsa of Govardhana). Met Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura in Vṛndāvana (1880); confirmed Śrī Caitanya's birthplace (Yogapīṭha) at Māyāpura and revealed Śrīvāsa-aṅgana; lived at Koladvīpa and from 1893 at Surabhi-kuñja, Godruma. Carried in a basket by his servant Bihārī dāsa in old age; said to have lived to about 135.

fields.name: Madhusūdana dāsa Bābājī
fields.aka: Siddha Madhusūdana dāsa Bābājī, Madhusūdana Dāsa Baba, Madhusūdana dāsa bābājī
fields.disappearance: Mārgaśīrṣa Śukla Aṣṭamī (Gauḍīya calendar), at Sūrya-kuṇḍa, Vraja
fields.notes: Siddha of Sūrya-kuṇḍa, guru of Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī; placed in the line of Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa through Uddhava dāsa (Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī's record). His own story: a kulīna boy who fled on his wedding night to Vṛndāvana and received a mantra by the Yamunā from an unknown mahānta of Gaṅgā-mātā's line; Siddha Kṛṣṇadāsa Bābā of Govardhana and Siddha Jayakṛṣṇa dāsa of Kāmyavana would not teach him without knowing his guru; at Rādhā-kuṇḍa Śrī Rādhā saved him, told him to live at Sūrya-kuṇḍa and never to give that mantra. Healed by Rādhā in the form of a Vraja girl; became known as «Siddha». Taught many but gave no dīkṣā.

fields.name: Vipina-vihārī Gosvāmī
fields.works: Daśa-mūla-rasa; Hari-bhakti-taraṅgiṇī; Harināmāmṛta-sindhu; translation of the Viṣṇu-sahasra-nāma
fields.notes: Gosvāmī of Bāghnāpāḍā (Bardhamān), of the family of Vaṁśīvadana Ṭhākura, a follower of Rāmāi Gosvāmī; alive in the early part of the 19th Śaka century (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna). Dīkṣā guru of Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura: Lord Caitanya told Bhaktivinoda in a dream that he would be his guru, and soon a letter came from him saying he was coming to initiate him.
